KAI is an Android keyboard (IME) written in Kotlin, a fork of Klava. Its main feature is AI support (an OpenAI-compatible API is required). Privacy: all input logic runs on the phone. Everything the keyboard writes to disk (learned words, pinned clipboard entries, the safe, the settings) is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key from the Android Keystore. Beyond that there are RU/EN dictionaries with word forms and bigrams (assets, built by the scripts in tools/), swipe typing with DTW alignment, smart key hitboxes, letter reordering when two thumbs type at once, clipboard history with pinning, a safe with a PIN, a \"PIN to delete\" and a fingerprint, a settings screen with search across every option, themes including a system one, and more.
KAI is a non-commercial app: no subscriptions, no analytics, no ads. Free software under the GNU GPL 3.0 or later (gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html). The source code is open.

Network: the only network code is data/ai/OpenAiCompatibleClient.kt. A request goes out only when you tap the buttons, with no redirects, no automatic retries and no logging interceptors; the key and the text are never logged. ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE is deliberately removed from the manifest - \"no network\" is detected from the request error. No ads, no analytics, no crash reports.
OkHttp, Okio, the Kotlin standard library - Apache License 2.0.

Dictionaries: word frequencies - FrequencyWords (Hermit Dave), the Taiga corpus (social media, T. Shavrina and O. Shapovalova) and the Leipzig Corpora Collection (web and news, Leipzig University), word forms - OpenCorpora; licence CC BY-SA 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Next-word suggestions are computed from Tatoeba sentences (tatoeba.org, licence CC BY 2.0 FR), OpenSubtitles subtitles (opensubtitles.org) from the OPUS collection, and from Taiga and the Leipzig Corpora Collection.

Emoji and their Russian and English names - Unicode, Inc. (emoji-test.txt, CLDR), Unicode License v3; Russian word forms for emoji search - OpenCorpora, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Swipe gesture point model - after the Android Open Source Project (LatinIME), Apache 2.0.

The safe locks as soon as you leave the Klava app or the keyboard closes. Get the PIN wrong many times and the pauses grow, but the entries are never erased by themselves.
Entering such a PIN instead of the real one silently erases the entries and opens the safe empty - to anyone watching it is an ordinary unlock. It works both when opening KAI and from the keyboard.
